discussionThreads.author: anlthms
discussionThreads.reason: New competitor claim with essential caveat preserved; current replies verified in logged-out Newest view. Recipe still unresolved.
discussionThreads.summary: mikelou1 reports an 87% local Qwen run under time constraints at roughly four-L4 speed (October 20 03:00 UTC). At 06:26 UTC the same author explicitly says 87% likely will not transfer, would be surprised by even 80%, and hopes for roughly 75%; those are expectations, not a submitted result. A later reply at 08:54 UTC says they are not very concerned about overfit because they get few runs. Other participants discuss throughput and the local-to-leaderboard gap. No complete recipe or independently verified new leaderboard score was supplied.
discussionThreads.title: Qwen3.8 or something else?

discussionThreads.author: cpmpml
discussionThreads.reason: Prior verified public staff explanation re-read; latest acknowledgment read, without independent measurement of the billing claim.
discussionThreads.summary: Kaggle Staff member Dustin says dataset download time does not count toward submission runtime. He explains that the live interactive quota display is an estimate and final usage corrects to container runtime when the session stops; data added while a container is running consumes quota. The staff explanation is publicly readable. Expanded CPMP acknowledgment says he had not checked the final adjustment and assumes staff is right; this is not independent confirmation.
discussionThreads.title: Are datasets download time include din submission sunning time?

discussionThreads.author: atelierzoe
discussionThreads.reason: Expanded mikelou1 branch read in Chrome and independently while logged out; public visibility established.
discussionThreads.summary: mikelou1 reports a score of 66% (about 60% local validation) in an expanded reply. Earlier replies deny using an NVARC ensemble and describe a kernel issue behind a lower result. The exact Qwen model variant and full recipe remain undisclosed. The current board independently shows the same entry at 66.39 and rank 13; the comment does not prove which change caused that gain.
discussionThreads.title: Qwen3.8-27B / Flash-Next: ARC-AGI-2 results within Kaggle’s compute limits?

discussionThreads.author: herbison
discussionThreads.reason: New Kaggle staff queue estimate verified in signed-in Chrome and logged-out public view.
discussionThreads.summary: In an October 16 reply, Kaggle staff member Dustin says ARC-2 queue delay has fallen to about three to five hours and most waiting is now actual submission runtime. He estimates turnaround below a day. Later participants still ask about long saves and runs; the staff estimate is dated, not a live service guarantee.
discussionThreads.title: Update on "Kaggle Error" Submissions & Queue Delays

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize reports verified Reflection Beam 1.0 scores: ARC-AGI-2 23.5% at $0.61/task and ARC-AGI-1 74.0% at $0.31/task. Best scores use xhigh reasoning; high reaches 20.0% on ARC-AGI-2 at about 43% lower cost.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: New official model evaluation. Linked result page independently read in Chrome: semi-private best scores match. This is benchmark evaluation, not a Kaggle team score.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize places Argon behind Astra’s 99.9% ARC-AGI-3 result. It reports 62% fewer actions than the human baseline on the 25 public games, matching or beating three speedrun records and coming within 10% on six others.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Keep the public-demo action comparison separate from the semi-private Verified score.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize says API issues prevented complete standard-harness testing: low reasoning completed 42/55 games for 49.8%; medium completed 46/55 for 46.3%; high completed 19/55 and no score was published. Reported scores retain partial credit across all 55 games. Provider adapter preserves opaque reasoning and permits automatic compaction; standard harness carries notes between turns. Costs use introductory $2 input/$10 output per million tokens.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Material limit on harness comparisons. Do not present incomplete standard-harness runs as a clean capability ceiling.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announces Gemini 4 Argon Verified results: ARC-AGI-3 97.5% at $4.8K with the provider adapter and 49.8% at $5.8K with the standard harness; ARC-AGI-2 91.3% at $0.32/task and ARC-AGI-1 98.5% at $0.16/task. It calls Google DeepMind the second frontier lab above 95% on ARC-AGI-3.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Consequential organizer result. Separate from Kaggle standings. Standard-harness API incompletion is essential context; primary results introduction says 91.2% on v2 while its table and announcement say 91.3%.

socialPosts.author: gklambauer
socialPosts.summary: Klambauer announces KronLSTM and links the new Kronecker Delta Rule paper. The authors propose a targeted association update for recurrent linear attention, report competitive long-context performance, and link open-source code and models. No ARC score is reported.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Research lead discovered in fses91’s separate Reposts feed. The primary arXiv abstract was checked independently; architecture claims remain attributed, and no Kaggle roster identity is inferred.

socialPosts.author: AInebosuke
socialPosts.summary: Translation of original Japanese: I improved my best score, though only a little. Following ARC3, I am aiming for the gold-medal band in ARC2 too. The Kaggle share text says rank 40.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Original Japanese read on actual public post. Direct X → nebosukeai.com → Kaggle isakatsuyoshi link verified, plus reciprocal Kaggle → X link. Public ARC2 board independently shows rank 40, 44.44, team 復活の混テキスト; gold is an ambition, not an awarded medal.

socialPosts.author: MindsAI_Jack
socialPosts.summary: Cole publicly confirms joining Mark Barney’s ARC-AGI-2 team, says he is excited, and says they will work hard through the last two weeks because the competition is strong. His quote contains Barney’s public ARC2 team announcement.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: New first-person team confirmation. Signed-in Chrome original post read; public post has no subscriber restriction. Exact public roster also shows jcole75 with markbarney, sonphamorg and scizical in ARC Mutants; this does not establish a joining date or score contribution.

socialPosts.author: 82deutschmark
socialPosts.summary: Mark Barney publicly welcomes Jack Cole to his ARC-AGI-2 team, using a Professor X metaphor, and states an ambition to reach gold. The post has ARC Mutants artwork. The announcement explicitly concerns ARC2; it does not add Cole to ARC3 Team Turducken.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Fresh public first-person confirmation supporting the commissioned ARC Mutants dispatch. Gold is an ambition, not an awarded medal.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize says Beam costs use Baseten pricing of $1.30 input and $4.30 output per million tokens. ARC-AGI-3 results are pending.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Keeps the cost basis and absence of ARC-AGI-3 results explicit.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize links its leaderboard, public reproduction repository, testing policy and full Beam 1.0 results.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Primary follow-up with reproducibility and policy links; group with the Beam announcement.

socialPosts.author: tufalabs
socialPosts.summary: Tufa says its two NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks are live in Stockholm; credits DELTA for installation and T.Loop for hosting and links a deployment video. Actual public post read.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Contender infrastructure announcement; no evidence here ties this equipment to a specific score or competition run.

socialPosts.author: JFPuget
socialPosts.summary: Puget says AI agents now run all his training experiments, while he still reads their harness code. He says agents tend to overengineer, retain unnecessary compatibility code and require human direction. Actual public post expanded and read.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: First-person account of a competitor’s research workflow; no new ARC score claimed.

wireStories.headline: Jay Gautam climbs 1,751 places to 96th on ARC-2

sections.text: Jay Gautam climbed 1,751 places in the past day, from 1847th to 96th, at a score of 34.03 after a gain of 6.25.
The move lifts Jay Gautam into the top 100 of a board with 3,142 teams, while the gold places still start at 66.53.

wireStories.headline: kibuna climbs from 55th to 31st on ARC-2

sections.text: kibuna gained 14.16 to 54.72 in the past day, moving from 55th to 31st on the ARC-2 board.
The gain is large, but the score is still well short of the gold line at 66.53, so the jump is a move up the table rather than a medal threat yet.

wireStories.headline: matu997 takes the last ARC-2 gold place as the line rises to 66.53

sections.text: matu997 moved from 18th to 16th at 66.53, gaining 2.22, and now holds the last of the 16 gold places.
The gold line itself rose 0.97 in the past day to 66.53. NguyenThanhNhan, 17th at 65.97, is 0.56 short and is the first team outside gold.
